reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first four premises regarding activity, stability, and homogeneity of high-entropy spinel oxides for CO oxidation. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a Pt-group metal support role with reduced noble metal loading, a premise not addressed by the cited study, which tested the spinel oxides themselves as catalysts without noble metals.
premises: High configurational entropy in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity under dry, lean conditions.
A 7-metal high-entropy spinel oxide (HESO) shows a 63% lower T10 for CO oxidation vs. a 4-metal spinel (MESO).
The 7-metal HESO exhibits better long-term stability (4.7% vs. 12.2% activity decrease over 14 h) than the 4-metal MESO.
High-entropy spinel oxides can be synthesized with a homogeneous distribution of elements.
The improved performance and stability can be extended to a support for dispersed Pt-group metals with reduced loading.
